F-DG6-640 is fixed. A restricted token copied from the published version into its draft, or from another rule, is now refused with 422 `automation_rule.restricted_token_stale`. It no longer silently stands for a different hidden record. All acceptance checks exited 0, and the changes are uncommitted for you to integrate.

**What changed**
- **Token format:** the token is now `[restricted:<tag>:<k>]`. The tag is 24 hex digits of an HMAC-SHA256 over the issuing rule-version row's id and its row version. A save resolves a token only when its tag matches the row being replaced at the If-Match version. Any other tag, and any token in the old `[restricted:<version>:<k>]` form, gets the 422.
- **Where the key comes from:** the existing configuration has no general server-side key, so I didn't reuse the OIDC secret or the DB credentials. A per-process key would break across replicas and restarts. A new deployment secret would be an ops change and would need a dev default in the repo. Instead, new migration **`0127_p6_automation_restricted_token_key.sql`** gives each rule-version row its own random 32-byte key. The key is fixed once the row is created and is never served, audited or logged. ADR-0051 part A records this reasoning.
- **Deploy effect:** every token issued before 0127 becomes stale. The editor shows its "changed, re-apply" message and reloads. No stored data changes.
- **Endpoints added:** none. The token text changes in the rule-version and rule reads; the update operation gets the tag check.
- **Web:** the editor logic is unchanged and treats the token as opaque. A new jsdom test (en and ar) confirms the "changed, re-apply" message shows on the new 422.
- **User-facing text:** the stale-token problem text said "issued from an earlier version of this draft", which is now only one of three cases. I corrected it in the API and in the en/ar `problems.json`.
- **Records:** ADR-0051 part A rewritten (with a note quoting the old text), the OpenAPI descriptions and the data dictionary updated. I also added one sentence to ADR-0043, whose token-format statement had become untrue.

**Tests**
- **Before the fix**, on unmodified code: the domain reviewer's probes (i) and (j) failed. My new cases (a) opaque tag, (b) published→draft, (c) cross-rule and (g) old-format token failed too.
- **After the fix:** everything passes. Last run on the final tree: 87/87.
- **Regression guards:** the three cases the brief asked for on already-fixed behaviour (re-save of the same draft, re-save after a 409, normal round trip) pass both before and after, because F-DG6-580 was already fixed by BE-Z14. So they don't have a failing before-fix log; the handback says so.
- **Probe adaptation:** the domain probe's (g) and (e) assert the old token text literally. For the after-fix run I moved only those token strings to the new form; the diff is in the evidence folder.

|---|---|
| `node tools/gates/validate.mjs --historical --stage DG5` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm -r build`, `pnpm lint`, prettier check | exit 0 |
| `pnpm openapi:lint` | exit 0 (932 operations) |
| `pnpm test`, locale unset and `C.UTF-8` | exit 0 both: 2902 / 2105 / 259 passed, 2 skipped (all 3 Vitest projects) |
| Related API integration files (automation, contract, inventory, sweeps, jobs, operations including the BE-Z6 race) | 25 files, 265/265 |
| Worker integration files (failure queue, job runs, outbox, starters, …) + QA a13 starter jobs | 7 files, 59/59 |
| e2e `a22-p6-operability` + `a13-automation-recovery`, real stack, chromium-en and chromium-ar | 4 passed |

My first OpenAPI lint attempt exited 254 because my shell loop cut the command to `pnpm openapi`; it wasn't the lint. The correct re-run passed, and the log says so.

**Not covered**
- No pending-operations change: no operation was added or moved.
- I didn't re-run the domain reviewer's Playwright probe; it asserts the old token text.
- Two of my test assertions could, very rarely, give a false result: about 1 in 77,000 for the adapted probe (evidence copy only) and 3 × 10⁻⁷ for z15 case (a).
- If another task ships 0127 first, renumbering also needs a few labels and comments updated; the handback lists them.
